title: RS_TileExplode
description: >
  Splits the input raster into a grid of fixed-size tiles and emits one row per
  tile with top-level `x`, `y`, and `tile` columns.
kernels:
  - returns: raster
    args:
    - raster
    - name: width
      type: integer
      description: Tile width in pixels. Must be >= 1.
    - name: height
      type: integer
      description: Tile height in pixels. Must be >= 1.
    - name: pad_with_no_data
      type: boolean
      description: >
        Optional (default false). When true, pad the last partial row/column of
        tiles to the full tile size with a nodata fill; when false the smaller
        edge tile is emitted as-is.
    - name: no_data_value
      type: double
      description: >
        Optional. The value written to padded pixels (only valid with
        `pad_with_no_data = true`); defaults to the band's own nodata value, or
        the band data type's minimum if it has none. It is an error if it does
        not fit the band's data type.
  - returns: raster
    args:
    - raster
    - name: band_index
      type: integer
      description: A single 1-based band index to include in each tile.
    - name: width
      type: integer
    - name: height
      type: integer
    - name: pad_with_no_data
      type: boolean
    - name: no_data_value
      type: double
  - returns: raster
    args:
    - raster
    - name: band_indices
      type: array
      description: >
        `Array[Int]` of 1-based band indices to include in each tile, in the
        given order.
    - name: width
      type: integer
    - name: height
      type: integer
    - name: pad_with_no_data
      type: boolean
    - name: no_data_value
      type: double

::: callout-warning
**Experimental.** This function is experimental; its behavior may change without notice.
:::

## Description

`RS_TileExplode` cuts a raster into a grid of `width` x `height` tiles and emits
**one row per tile**, mirroring Sedona Spark's `RS_TileExplode` generator. It is
the row-multiplying form of `RS_Tile`, which returns every tile of a raster in a
single `List` cell that you would otherwise `UNNEST`. `RS_TileExplode(rast, w, h)`
and `UNNEST(RS_Tile(rast, w, h))` produce byte-identical tiles in the same order.

The generator appends three **top-level** columns to the query's other selected
columns:

- `x`: the tile's grid column (0-based), counting from the left.
- `y`: the tile's grid row (0-based), counting from the top.
- `tile`: the tile raster, with a geotransform shifted to the tile's own origin.

The grid is `ceil(width / tile_width)` columns by `ceil(height / tile_height)`
rows, iterated row-major (`y` then `x`). When the raster does not divide evenly,
the last column and row of tiles are partial: with `pad_with_no_data = false` the
smaller edge tile is emitted as-is, and with `pad_with_no_data = true` those tiles
are padded to the full tile size with a nodata fill. When the band(s) have no
nodata value, `no_data_value` supplies one.

When no band argument is given, every band is included. A scalar `band_index`
selects a single band; `band_indices` selects an ordered subset of bands. Band
indices are 1-based. A null or untileable raster contributes zero rows.

`RS_TileExplode` is a generator, so it may appear only as a single top-level
column of a `SELECT` (alongside pass-through columns). Nesting it inside another
expression, placing it in `WHERE`/`HAVING`/`GROUP BY`, or using two generators in
one `SELECT` is a plan-time error. Its raster argument must be a **column**
reference — tile the rasters of a table (or a derived table such as
`(SELECT RS_Example() AS rast)`), not a constant raster expression.

::: callout-note
`RS_TileExplode` **copies the raster**: every tile carries its own pixels, so
tiling copies the full raster spread across the tiles. A small tile size produces
many tiles (a `1 x 1` tile size yields one tile per pixel).
:::

## Examples

Explode every band of a raster column into a 2x2 grid of 32x16 tiles, counting
the rows so the example output stays small rather than printing every tile
raster:

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_tiles
FROM (SELECT RS_TileExplode(rast, 32, 16) FROM (SELECT RS_Example() AS rast));
```

Explode every band, padding the edge tiles to the full 40x20 size with a nodata
fill of 0:

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_tiles
FROM (SELECT RS_TileExplode(rast, 40, 20, true, 0.0) FROM (SELECT RS_Example() AS rast));
```

Explode a single band (band 1) into 32x16 tiles:

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_tiles
FROM (SELECT RS_TileExplode(rast, 1, 32, 16) FROM (SELECT RS_Example() AS rast));
```

Explode an ordered subset of bands:

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_tiles
FROM (SELECT RS_TileExplode(rast, make_array(1, 3), 32, 16) FROM (SELECT RS_Example() AS rast));
```

Pass-through columns are replicated across every tile row. Here `id` rides along
with each of the exploded tiles, so grouping the exploded rows by `id` counts one
raster's tiles:

```sql
SELECT id, COUNT(*) AS num_tiles
FROM (
  SELECT id, RS_TileExplode(rast, 32, 16)
  FROM (SELECT 7 AS id, RS_Example() AS rast)
)
GROUP BY id;
```
